Topic: Tutor setup - paste this at the start of every new chat
Prompt_Text: You are my personal German tutor. I'm a [YOUR NATIVE LANGUAGE] speaker following a 52-week plan from A1 to B2, studying about 10-15 hours per week. I'll tell you which week I'm on and paste that week's lesson prompt. Follow these rules in every lesson: (1) Explain grammar in English; keep German examples at my current level and translate new ones. (2) Give every noun with article and plural (der Tisch, -e), and every verb with its irregular forms, separable prefix and the case/preposition it takes. (3) Recycle vocabulary and grammar from earlier weeks in examples and dialogues. (4) Present vocabulary as a table: German | English | example sentence, so I can import it into Anki. (5) Mark the 20 most important words of each lesson with a star. (6) Split long lessons into numbered parts and ask me before continuing, so nothing gets cut off. (7) End each lesson with a 10-question quiz and wait for my answers before showing solutions. (8) When I write German, show my sentence, the corrected sentence and a one-line explanation of each error, and keep track of my recurring mistakes. (9) Use Standard German, but point out Austrian and Swiss differences when relevant.
Practice_Prompt: WEEKLY ROUTINE (follow-up prompts to reuse every week in the same chat): Day 1 - send the week's Prompt_Text (the lesson). Day 2 - 'Give me 20 drill exercises on this week's grammar with increasing difficulty; answers at the end.' Day 3 - send the week's Practice_Prompt. Day 4 - 'Write a 150-300 word text at my level using this week's vocabulary, then ask me 5 comprehension questions.' Day 5 - 'Here is my writing on this week's topic: [text]. Correct it with explanations.' Day 6 - 'Quiz me on 30 words from this week and 10 from previous weeks; repeat the ones I get wrong.' Day 7 - 'Summarize my most frequent mistakes this week and give me 10 sentences to fix them.'
Self_Study_Instructions: Fill in the [brackets]; Install Anki (free) for vocabulary; Find a Tandem/HelloTalk partner; Bookmark the free official Goethe practice tests for A1, A2, B1 and B2

Vocabulary_Target: Greetings, farewells, introductions, countries & languages, alphabet
Grammar_Focus: Personal pronouns; sein & heißen; verb in position 2; W-questions (Wie, Wo, Woher, Was)
Cultural_Focus: German-speaking countries (DACH); du vs. Sie; regional greetings (Moin, Grüß Gott, Servus, Grüezi)
Prompt_Text: Week 1, A1, absolute beginner. Teach me: (1) the German alphabet and the 12 sounds English speakers struggle with most (ä, ö, ü, ß, ch in ich/ach, r, ei vs. ie, eu/äu, z, w, v, st/sp at word start), each with 3 example words and simple pronunciation tips; (2) 60 words for greetings, farewells, introductions, countries and languages; (3) personal pronouns and the present tense of sein and heißen, plus the W-questions Wie? Wo? Woher? Was?; (4) 10 short dialogues (5 formal with Sie, 5 informal with du) set in a hostel, an office, a university, a café and a video call. Then explain when Germans, Austrians and Swiss use du vs. Sie, and the regional greetings Moin, Grüß Gott, Servus and Grüezi. Finish with the 5 most typical beginner mistakes and a 10-question quiz.
Practice_Prompt: Role-play: you are a new coworker in Munich meeting me on my first day. Speak only simple A1 German, use Sie, and ask me 6 questions about my name, origin, languages and where I live. After the conversation, correct every mistake I made and give me the corrected version of each answer.
Self_Study_Instructions: Shadow pronunciation 15 min/day (DW Nicos Weg A1, first 5 episodes); Label a blank map of the DACH countries and capitals in German; Record a 30-second self-introduction and compare it with a native speaker; Set up Anki and import this week's vocabulary table

Vocabulary_Target: Numbers 0-1,000, clock times, days, months, seasons, dates, prices, phone numbers
Grammar_Focus: Present tense of regular verbs; verb-second rule after time expressions; am / um / im
Cultural_Focus: Punctuality; 24-hour clock in daily life; opening hours; public holidays by state
Prompt_Text: Week 2, A1. Teach me numbers 0-1,000 (with the 'reversed' tens like einundzwanzig and memory tricks), official and colloquial clock time (14:30 vs. halb drei, Viertel nach/vor), days, months, seasons and dates (am ersten Mai). Explain present-tense conjugation of regular verbs with 15 high-frequency verbs (wohnen, arbeiten, lernen, kommen, machen...), including the -est/-et rule for arbeiten/finden, and 'am / um / im' for time. Give me 70 words in total, 10 dialogues (making an appointment, asking opening hours, giving a phone number, buying a train ticket for a specific time), and explain German punctuality norms and the public holidays (Feiertage) that differ by state. Include an exercise where you write numbers as words and I write the digits.
Practice_Prompt: Dictate 15 random times, dates, prices and phone numbers to me written out in German words (e.g. 'Viertel vor acht'), one at a time. I answer in digits. Track my score, then give me 5 harder ones on the types I got wrong.
Self_Study_Instructions: Say every clock time you see in German for a week; Switch your phone's calendar and clock to German; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes; Look up which German public holidays fall in the next 3 months and in which states

Vocabulary_Target: Family members, relationships, age, birthdays, personal data on forms
Grammar_Focus: haben; possessive articles (mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr) in the nominative; yes/no vs. W-questions
Cultural_Focus: Family structures; never congratulate before a birthday; forms and the Anmeldung
Prompt_Text: Week 3, A1. Teach me 70 words for family members, relationships, age, birthdays and personal data (Vorname, Nachname, Geburtsdatum, Familienstand, Wohnort). Explain the conjugation of haben and all possessive articles in the nominative (mein/meine, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr) with a clear table and the 'his vs. her' trap for English speakers. Contrast yes/no questions (verb first) with W-questions. Give 10 dialogues: showing family photos, a birthday invitation, a registration form at a language school, chatting with a neighbor. Explain German family culture: smaller families, the custom of never congratulating someone before their birthday, and why there are so many forms (Anmeldung). Add a fill-in-the-form exercise with a fictional person.
Practice_Prompt: Describe a fictional family tree in German sentences, then ask me 10 questions about it (Wie heißt die Schwester von...? Wie alt ist...?). Afterwards ask me 5 questions about my real family and correct my answers.
Self_Study_Instructions: Draw your family tree with German labels and possessives; Fill in a sample German registration form online (practice only); Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes; Write 8 sentences about your family and post them on a language-exchange app for correction

Vocabulary_Target: Rooms, furniture, appliances, adjectives to describe a flat
Grammar_Focus: Noun gender rules (der/die/das by ending); 5 plural patterns; nominative definite/indefinite articles; kein vs. nicht
Cultural_Focus: Renting culture: Altbau/Neubau, WG, Kaltmiete vs. Warmmiete, Kaution, flats without kitchens
Prompt_Text: Week 4, A1. Teach me German noun gender with the most reliable rules (-ung/-heit/-keit/-ion = die, -chen/-lein = das, -er for people often der, etc.) and the 5 main plural patterns, with an honest note about exceptions. Then teach 80 words for rooms, furniture, appliances and describing a home (each noun with article and plural). Explain the nominative of definite and indefinite articles and when to use kein vs. nicht. Create 10 dialogues: viewing a flat, describing a room to a friend, a WG interview, reporting that something is broken. Explain German renting culture: why most people rent, Altbau vs. Neubau, WGs, Kaltmiete vs. Warmmiete, Kaution, and why kitchens are often not included. Give me a color-coding memory system (blue/red/green) for der/die/das.
Practice_Prompt: Describe a flat listing to me in A1 German (rooms, size, price). Then I'll ask you questions as if I want to rent it. After that, give me 20 nouns without articles and test me on der/die/das and the plural; explain each mistake using the gender rules.
Self_Study_Instructions: Put sticky notes with article + noun on 30 items at home; Browse WG-gesucht.de listings and pick out 20 words; Describe your own home in 10 sentences; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Topic: Food, Drinks & Eating Out; Accusative Case
Vocabulary_Target: Food, drinks, meals, quantities & packaging, restaurant phrases, taste
Grammar_Focus: Accusative case (den, einen, keinen); möchten; gern / lieber / am liebsten; stem-changing essen, nehmen
Cultural_Focus: Meal culture (Abendbrot, Kaffee und Kuchen), bakeries, tipping, paying separately, Pfand
Prompt_Text: Week 5, A1. Introduce the accusative case through food: show the article table (only masculine changes: der to den, ein to einen, kein to keinen) and the verbs that usually take an accusative object (haben, möchten, essen, trinken, nehmen, kaufen, brauchen). Teach the stem-changing verbs essen/nehmen and preferences with gern, lieber, am liebsten. Teach 90 food and drink words with articles, plus quantities (eine Flasche, ein Kilo, 200 Gramm). Create 10 dialogues: bakery, supermarket, ordering in a restaurant, paying (zusammen oder getrennt?), inviting a friend for dinner. Explain German meal culture (Abendbrot, Kaffee und Kuchen, Sunday Brötchen), tipping, splitting the bill, the Pfand bottle deposit, and regional dishes from Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
Practice_Prompt: Be a waiter in a Berlin restaurant. Give me a short German menu with prices, take my order, make one mistake with my order that I have to fix, and bring the bill. Then correct every accusative and word-order mistake I made.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write your weekly shopping list in German with articles; Cook one German or Austrian recipe from a German recipe site (e.g. chefkoch.de); Accusative drills 15 min/day; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Topic: Daily Routine; Separable Verbs & Word Order
Vocabulary_Target: Daily activities, frequency adverbs, parts of the day
Grammar_Focus: Separable verbs (aufstehen, einkaufen, anrufen, fernsehen); inversion after time expressions; frequency adverbs
Cultural_Focus: Daily rhythms, Feierabend, quiet hours (Ruhezeiten), Sunday rest, shop closing laws
Prompt_Text: Week 6, A1. Teach me separable verbs (aufstehen, anfangen, einkaufen, anrufen, fernsehen, aufräumen, mitkommen...) with the sentence bracket (Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf) and the rule that the verb stays in position 2 after a time expression (Am Morgen trinke ich Kaffee). Teach 80 words for daily routines, frequency (immer, oft, manchmal, nie) and parts of the day. Write 10 dialogues comparing the routines of a student, a shift-working nurse, a parent and a retiree. Explain German daily rhythms: early starts, Feierabend, quiet hours (Ruhezeiten), Sunday rest (Sonntagsruhe) and shop closing laws, and how Austria and Switzerland compare. Include an exercise where I reorder scrambled words into correct sentences.
Practice_Prompt: Ask me about my typical weekday and weekend in German, one question at a time (10 questions). Require at least 6 separable verbs. Afterwards, rewrite my answers as one corrected paragraph and highlight every word-order fix.
Self_Study_Instructions: Narrate your own actions aloud in German for 10 min/day; Write your daily schedule using 10 separable verbs; Compare German shop opening hours with your country's; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Vocabulary_Target: Clothes, colors, sizes, materials, shops, prices, payment
Grammar_Focus: Accusative personal pronouns (mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch); welcher / dieser; 'Wie gefällt dir...?' as a fixed phrase
Cultural_Focus: Cash culture, fast checkouts, returns (Umtausch), flea markets
Prompt_Text: Week 7, A1. Teach accusative personal pronouns (mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie/Sie) with substitution drills (Ich kaufe den Pullover - Ich kaufe ihn), plus welcher/welche/welches and dieser. Teach 'Wie gefällt dir/Ihnen...?' and 'Das steht dir' as fixed phrases. Give me 80 words for clothes, colors, sizes, materials, shops and payment. Create 10 dialogues: in a clothes shop, at the checkout (Bar oder mit Karte?), returning an item, bargaining at a Flohmarkt, online shopping. Explain German shopping culture: frequent cash payment, fast checkouts where you bag your own groceries, return rules, flea markets, and differences between Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
Practice_Prompt: Role-play: I'm in a clothing store in Vienna and you are the shop assistant. I need a winter jacket. Guide me through sizes, colors and price, and make me use accusative pronouns at least 5 times. Correct me afterwards.
Self_Study_Instructions: Describe what you're wearing every morning in German; Browse a German online shop in German and note 20 words; Accusative-pronoun drills 10 min/day; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Vocabulary_Target: Hobbies, sports, music, going out, invitations, accepting/declining
Grammar_Focus: Modal verbs (können, wollen, müssen, dürfen, sollen, mögen) + möchten; infinitive at the end
Cultural_Focus: Vereinskultur (clubs), planning social plans ahead, hiking, football, sauna etiquette
Prompt_Text: Week 8, A1. Teach all six modal verbs (können, wollen, müssen, dürfen, sollen, mögen) plus möchten, with their irregular singular forms and the sentence bracket (Ich kann gut schwimmen). Show their meanings clearly (ability, wish, obligation, permission, advice), including the trap 'muss nicht' = don't have to, not 'must not'. Teach 80 words for hobbies, sports, music, going out, and for making, accepting and declining invitations. Create 10 dialogues: planning a weekend, joining a sports club, declining politely, asking permission. Explain German Vereinskultur (there's a club for everything), how far ahead Germans plan social activities, and popular leisure activities in DACH (hiking, football, cycling, saunas and their etiquette).
Practice_Prompt: Invite me to 5 different activities in German via short text messages. I must accept or decline each with a reason using modal verbs. Then we switch: I invite you. Correct my modal-verb forms and word order at the end.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 15 sentences about what you can / must / want to do this week; Find a German club (Verein) website for your hobby and read its homepage; Listen to 1 episode of the Easy German Podcast; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Topic: City, Directions & Transport; Dative Prepositions & Imperative
Vocabulary_Target: Places in town, transport, directions, tickets
Grammar_Focus: Dative case with aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu; contractions (zum, zur, beim, vom); imperative (du, ihr, Sie)
Cultural_Focus: Deutsche Bahn, Deutschlandticket, fare dodging fines, cycling rules, Swiss train punctuality
Prompt_Text: Week 9, A1. Introduce the dative case through the city: the dative article table, the always-dative prepositions (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu) and contractions (zum, zur, beim, vom). Teach the imperative for du, ihr and Sie (Gehen Sie geradeaus! Nimm die U2!). Teach 80 words for places in town, transport, directions and tickets. Create 10 dialogues: asking for directions, buying a ticket from a machine, a delayed-train announcement, giving directions to a tourist, taking a taxi. Explain transport culture in DACH: Deutsche Bahn and its delays, the Deutschlandticket, ticket inspections and fines for riding without a ticket, cycling rules and bike lanes, Swiss train punctuality, and why Germans wait at red pedestrian lights.
Practice_Prompt: Give me a simple map of a fictional German town in text form (a list of streets and buildings). Ask me to explain the way from the station to 5 places using imperatives and dative prepositions. Then you give me directions to 3 places and I say where I end up. Correct all case errors.
Self_Study_Instructions: Plan a fictional trip from Berlin to Munich on bahn.de in German; Use Google Maps in German for a week; Dative-preposition drills 10 min/day; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Vocabulary_Target: Body parts, symptoms, illnesses, doctor's office, pharmacy, appointments
Grammar_Focus: Dative personal pronouns (mir, dir, ihm, ihr...); 'Mir tut... weh'; sollen for passing on advice; imperative review
Cultural_Focus: Krankenkasse, family doctor (Hausarzt) first, Apotheke vs. Drogerie, sick notes, 112 and 116 117
Prompt_Text: Week 10, A1. Teach 80 words for body parts, symptoms, illnesses, the doctor's office and the pharmacy. Teach dative personal pronouns (mir, dir, ihm, ihr, uns, euch, ihnen/Ihnen) through high-frequency expressions: Mir tut der Kopf weh, Mir ist schlecht, Wie geht es dir?, Gute Besserung. Practice sollen for passing on advice (Der Arzt sagt, ich soll viel trinken) and review the imperative. Create 10 dialogues: calling a doctor's office for an appointment, at the doctor, at the pharmacy, calling in sick at work. Explain the healthcare system: public vs. private health insurance, the insurance card, going to a Hausarzt first, Apotheke vs. Drogerie (dm, Rossmann), the sick note (Krankschreibung), and the numbers 112 and 116 117.
Practice_Prompt: Role-play: you are the receptionist at a family doctor's practice. I call to make an appointment because I'm sick. Then you become the doctor and ask me about my symptoms. Use only A1 language. Afterwards, correct my dative pronouns and verb forms.
Self_Study_Instructions: Label a body diagram in German; Learn by heart the phrases for calling in sick at work; Read the product pages of a German online pharmacy; Nicos Weg A1: next 5 episodes

Topic: A1 Review & Goethe A1 Mock Exam
Vocabulary_Target: Review of all A1 vocabulary (~770 words)
Grammar_Focus: All A1 grammar: present tense, gender & plurals, nominative/accusative/dative basics, modals, separable verbs, imperative, word order
Cultural_Focus: Cultural check: everyday life in DACH
Prompt_Text: Week 11, A1 review. Based on the Goethe-Zertifikat A1 (Start Deutsch 1) format, create a full mock exam with four parts: Hören (as transcripts I can read aloud or record), Lesen, Schreiben (a short form plus a ~30-word message) and Sprechen (introduce yourself, ask and answer questions on a topic, make and react to requests). Then give me a one-page summary of all A1 grammar (present tense, gender and plurals, nominative/accusative/dative, modal verbs, separable verbs, imperative, word order), a 100-word review of the most-forgotten vocabulary from weeks 1-10, and a 15-question quiz on everyday culture in DACH. Don't show answers until I submit. Afterwards, analyze my errors by category and give me a list of my 5 weakest points to fix before starting A2.
Practice_Prompt: Simulate the A1 speaking exam (Sprechen parts 1-3) with me as the candidate, one task at a time. Score me with the Goethe criteria and explain what would cost me points.
Self_Study_Instructions: Take the free official Goethe A1 practice test (Übungssatz) online, timed; Re-review all Anki cards marked 'hard'; Record a 2-minute monologue about yourself and listen for errors; Watch a German film with German subtitles as a reward

Vocabulary_Target: Weekend activities, past time expressions (gestern, letzte Woche, vor zwei Jahren)
Grammar_Focus: Perfekt with haben and sein; regular participles (ge-...-t); when to use sein (movement, change of state)
Cultural_Focus: Monday small talk at work, what's private, long weekends (Brückentage)
Prompt_Text: Week 12, A2. Teach the Perfekt (spoken past): haben/sein + Partizip II, regular participles (gemacht, gekauft, gearbeitet), and the rule for sein (movement from A to B and change of state: gefahren, gegangen, aufgestanden, plus the exception geblieben). Give me the 40 most common verbs with their participles and 50 new words for weekend activities and past time expressions (gestern, vorgestern, letzte Woche, vor zwei Jahren). Create 10 dialogues: Monday-morning small talk at the office, a phone call with a parent, a text chat about a party. Explain how Germans talk about the weekend at work (what's fine to share, what's too private), Brückentage, and typical weekend activities. Add an exercise converting present-tense sentences into Perfekt.
Practice_Prompt: Ask me 'Was hast du am Wochenende gemacht?' and keep asking follow-up questions for 10 turns like a curious colleague. Then rewrite my answers correctly and list every participle and auxiliary I got wrong.
Self_Study_Instructions: Keep a 5-sentence Perfekt diary every evening; Make Anki cards: infinitive - participle + haben/sein; Start DW Nicos Weg A2 or Easy German street interviews; Write a message to a language partner about your weekend

Vocabulary_Target: Travel types, accommodation, luggage, sightseeing, travel problems
Grammar_Focus: Irregular participles by vowel pattern; participles of separable (eingekauft), inseparable (besucht) and -ieren verbs (telefoniert)
Cultural_Focus: Holiday culture: generous paid leave, Mallorca/Italy/Baltic Sea, camping, hiking holidays
Prompt_Text: Week 13, A2. Teach the 60 most important irregular participles grouped by vowel pattern (e.g. geschrieben/geblieben, getrunken/gefunden), and the participle rules for separable verbs (eingekauft, angekommen), inseparable verbs (besucht, verstanden, erzählt) and -ieren verbs (telefoniert, studiert). Teach 80 words for travel, accommodation, luggage, sightseeing and travel problems. Create 10 dialogues: telling a friend about a holiday, a hotel check-in that went wrong, a lost suitcase at the airport, booking a holiday flat. Explain German holiday culture: generous paid leave, favorite destinations (Mallorca, Italy, the Baltic Sea), camping and caravans, hiking holidays, and the towel-on-the-sunbed stereotype vs. reality.
Practice_Prompt: Pretend we're friends meeting after my summer holiday. Ask me about my trip with 10 follow-up questions, including one problem I must describe (delayed train, bad hotel). Then list my wrong participles with the correct form and a memory hook for each.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write a 150-word holiday story in Perfekt; Drill the irregular verb list in a verb-trainer app 10 min/day; Read one German travel blog post; Plan a dream trip in German and post it for correction

Topic: Childhood & School Memories; Präteritum of sein, haben & Modals
Vocabulary_Target: Childhood, school subjects, school life, grades, toys
Grammar_Focus: Präteritum of sein, haben and modal verbs (war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, durfte); früher vs. heute
Cultural_Focus: School system (Grundschule, Gymnasium, Realschule...), Schultüte, grading scales in DE/AT/CH
Prompt_Text: Week 14, A2. Teach the Präteritum of sein, haben and all modal verbs (war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte, mochte) and explain why Germans use these in Präteritum even when speaking, while most other verbs stay in Perfekt. Teach 'früher... heute' contrasts. Teach 80 words for childhood, school subjects, school life and grades. Create 10 dialogues: talking about childhood with a partner, a parent-teacher conversation, comparing school memories from different countries. Explain the German school system (Grundschule, then Gymnasium / Realschule / Hauptschule / Gesamtschule, Abitur), the Schultüte on the first school day, and the grading scales (Germany: 1 is best; Switzerland: 6 is best; Austria: 1-5).
Practice_Prompt: Interview me about my childhood like a podcast host: 10 questions about where I lived, what I could / had to / wanted to do, and my school. Then correct my mix of Präteritum and Perfekt and explain which form a native speaker would choose.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 'Meine Kindheit' (150 words) using war / hatte / modal verbs; Watch a German-language video about the German school system; Compare your school system with Germany's in 8 sentences; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Moving house, placing furniture, household chores, building rules
Grammar_Focus: Wechselpräpositionen (in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen): Wo? + dative vs. Wohin? + accusative; stellen/stehen, legen/liegen, setzen/sitzen, hängen
Cultural_Focus: Registering your address, Hausordnung, quiet hours, cleaning rotas, introducing yourself to neighbors
Prompt_Text: Week 15, A2. Teach the nine two-way prepositions (in, an, auf, über, unter, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) with the rule Wo? (dative, location) vs. Wohin? (accusative, direction), and the verb pairs stellen/stehen, legen/liegen, setzen/sitzen, hängen/hängen. Use clear visual descriptions (e.g. a room before and after moving in). Teach 80 words for moving house, placing furniture, household chores and building rules. Create 10 dialogues: helping a friend move, telling movers where to put things, a conflict with a neighbor about noise, reading the house rules. Explain German moving culture: registering your address (Anmeldung) within two weeks, the Hausordnung, quiet hours, stairwell cleaning rotas, and introducing yourself to neighbors.
Practice_Prompt: Describe a messy room in German with 10 objects in specific places. Then give me 10 instructions where I say where I put each thing (Ich stelle die Lampe auf den Tisch). Then ask me 'Wo ist...?' for each. Correct every dative/accusative mistake with a one-line reason.
Self_Study_Instructions: Describe where 20 objects are in your room (Wo?) and where you put them (Wohin?); Read a real German Hausordnung example online; Two-way-preposition drills 15 min/day; Watch an Easy German video about living in Germany

Topic: Weather, Seasons & Nature; weil / dass / wenn
Vocabulary_Target: Weather, seasons, nature, landscapes, outdoor activities
Grammar_Focus: Subordinate clauses with weil, dass, wenn (verb at the end); starting with the subordinate clause; weil vs. denn
Cultural_Focus: Hiking and the Alps, beer gardens, swimming lakes, 'Hitzefrei', the Föhn wind
Prompt_Text: Week 16, A2. Teach subordinate clauses with weil, dass and wenn and the verb-final rule (..., weil das Wetter schön ist), including separable and modal verbs at the end (..., weil ich früh aufstehen muss) and starting the sentence with the subordinate clause (Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause). Contrast weil (verb last) with denn (normal word order). Teach 80 words for weather, seasons, nature, landscapes and outdoor activities. Create 10 dialogues: planning a hike depending on the weather, weather small talk, a weather forecast, cancelling a barbecue. Explain DACH outdoor culture: hiking and the Alps, beer gardens, swimming lakes, 'Hitzefrei' at school, the Föhn wind, and the saying 'Es gibt kein schlechtes Wetter, nur falsche Kleidung'.
Practice_Prompt: Ask me 10 'Warum...?' and 'Was machst du, wenn...?' questions about weather and seasons. I must answer with weil / wenn / dass clauses. Score each sentence for word order and give the corrected version.
Self_Study_Instructions: Read the German weather forecast every morning and summarize it in 2 sentences; Write 10 'Wenn..., dann...' sentences about your plans; Listen to 1 episode of the 'Slow German' podcast; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Holidays, celebrations, gifts, congratulations, invitations
Grammar_Focus: Verbs with dative (helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören, gratulieren, schmecken); verbs with dative + accusative (geben, schenken, zeigen) and object order
Cultural_Focus: Advent and Christmas markets, Christmas on the 24th, Easter, Karneval/Fasching, Oktoberfest, Silvester, gift etiquette
Prompt_Text: Week 17, A2. Teach verbs that take only a dative object (helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören, gratulieren, schmecken, passen, antworten) and verbs with both dative and accusative (geben, schenken, zeigen, bringen, erklären, empfehlen), including object order (Ich schenke meiner Mutter einen Schal / Ich schenke ihn ihr). Teach 80 words for holidays, celebrations, gifts, congratulations and invitations. Create 10 dialogues: buying a birthday gift, a written invitation and RSVP, at a Christmas market, at a Karneval party, on New Year's Eve. Explain the festival calendar in DACH: Advent and the Weihnachtsmarkt, Christmas Eve on the 24th, Nikolaus, Easter traditions, Karneval/Fasching, Oktoberfest, Silvester customs ('Dinner for One'), the Day of German Unity, and gift etiquette (bring something when invited, flowers in odd numbers).
Practice_Prompt: Give me a list of 6 people (my boss, my host family, a child...) and their interests. I say what I give each person and why, using dative + accusative. Then write me a German party invitation and I reply to it. Correct object order and cases.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write a German birthday card and a thank-you note; Watch a short German documentary about a German festival (e.g. DW Doku); Make a German holiday calendar for the year; Daily Anki review

Topic: Describing People & Appearance; Adjective Endings I
Vocabulary_Target: Appearance, body features, clothing styles, personality
Grammar_Focus: Adjective endings after definite articles (weak declension: -e / -en); predicative vs. attributive adjectives
Cultural_Focus: Fashion attitudes, practicality, workplace dress codes, traditional dress (Dirndl, Lederhose)
Prompt_Text: Week 18, A2. Teach adjective endings after definite articles (weak declension: only -e or -en) with one clear table and a simple rule of thumb, contrasting predicative adjectives (Der Mann ist groß - no ending) with attributive ones (der große Mann). Practice in nominative, accusative and dative. Teach 80 words for appearance, body features, clothing styles and personality. Create 10 dialogues: describing a suspect to the police, finding a friend in a crowd, a fashion-shop conversation, gossiping about a TV character. Explain German attitudes to fashion and appearance: practicality (the outdoor-jacket stereotype), Berlin street style, workplace dress codes, and traditional dress (Dirndl, Lederhose) and when people actually wear it.
Practice_Prompt: Describe 5 people in an imaginary photo to me using adjectives. Then I describe 5 people (friends or famous people) and you guess who. Collect all my adjective-ending errors in a table: my version / correct version / rule.
Self_Study_Instructions: Describe 10 people in photos using adjective endings after definite articles; Adjective-ending drills 15 min/day (the hardest A2 topic - be patient); Watch one episode of 'Extra auf Deutsch' with German subtitles; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Friendship, relationships, feelings, character traits, dating
Grammar_Focus: Adjective endings after ein/kein/possessives (mixed) and with no article (strong); one combined decision method
Cultural_Focus: Friendship 'coconut' metaphor, Bekannte vs. Freunde, Stammtisch, dating and splitting the bill
Prompt_Text: Week 19, A2. Teach adjective endings after ein/kein/possessive articles (mixed declension) and with no article (strong declension: guter Wein, mit kaltem Wasser). Then give me ONE combined overview of all three tables with a step-by-step decision method I can apply to any sentence. Teach 80 words for friendship, relationships, feelings and character traits. Create 10 dialogues: describing your best friend, a dating-app profile, giving advice to a friend, an argument and making up. Explain German friendship culture: the 'coconut' metaphor (hard to get in, loyal once inside), Bekannte vs. Freunde, the Stammtisch, dating norms and splitting the bill, and being direct about feelings.
Practice_Prompt: Write me a short dating-app profile in German with 10 gaps for adjective endings. Then ask me to write my own profile (8 sentences with adjectives). Correct it and explain each ending using your step-by-step method.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write a 150-word description of your best friend; Mixed adjective-ending drills 15 min/day; Join an online German conversation group or Tandem session for 30 min; Daily Anki review

Topic: Work & Job Applications; Reflexive Verbs & Verbs with Prepositions
Vocabulary_Target: Jobs, workplace, applications, CV, interviews
Grammar_Focus: Reflexive verbs with accusative/dative pronouns; verbs with fixed prepositions (sich freuen auf/über, sich interessieren für, warten auf); Worauf? / Auf wen?
Cultural_Focus: Application culture (tabular CV, cover letter, Arbeitszeugnis), probation period, Feierabend, du vs. Sie at work
Prompt_Text: Week 20, A2. Teach reflexive verbs with accusative and dative reflexive pronouns (Ich wasche mich / Ich wasche mir die Hände) and 25 common reflexive verbs. Then teach 25 verbs with fixed prepositions (sich freuen auf/über, sich interessieren für, warten auf, denken an, sich bewerben um/bei, sprechen über) and how to ask about them (Worauf wartest du? Auf wen?). Teach 80 words for jobs, workplaces, applications, CVs and interviews. Create 10 dialogues: a job interview, a first day at work, asking a colleague for help, asking HR about vacation. Explain German application culture: the tabular Lebenslauf (often with a photo), the Anschreiben, the Arbeitszeugnis and its coded language, the Probezeit, working hours and Feierabend, and du vs. Sie in startups vs. traditional companies.
Practice_Prompt: Run a 10-question job interview with me in German for a job in my real field, using formal Sie. Afterwards, give feedback on my language (reflexive verbs, prepositions) and on my answers as a German HR manager would.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write your Lebenslauf in German (tabular format); Learn 25 verb + preposition pairs in Anki; Read 3 German job ads in your field (e.g. on stepstone.de); Record your answers to 5 common interview questions

Vocabulary_Target: City life, countryside, geography, describing places
Grammar_Focus: Comparative and superlative (am ...sten / der ...ste); umlaut changes; irregulars (gut, viel, gern, hoch, nah); als vs. wie
Cultural_Focus: Portraits of Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Vienna, Zürich; regional rivalries and stereotypes
Prompt_Text: Week 21, A2. Teach comparative and superlative forms (both am ...sten and der/die/das ...ste with adjective endings), umlaut changes (alt - älter), the irregulars (gut, viel, gern, hoch, nah) and als vs. wie (größer als / so groß wie). Teach 80 words for cities, countryside, geography and describing places. Create 10 dialogues: choosing which city to move to, comparing two flats, a quiz show about DACH superlatives (longest river, highest mountain), comparing prices. Give me a cultural portrait of Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Cologne, Vienna and Zürich, plus the friendly regional rivalries and the North/South and East/West stereotypes in Germany (and which ones are outdated).
Practice_Prompt: Let's debate in simple German: 'Stadt oder Land - wo lebt man besser?' You take the opposite side to mine. Make me use at least 8 comparatives or superlatives. Then correct and upgrade my sentences.
Self_Study_Instructions: Compare your hometown with a German city in 12 sentences; Watch an Easy German or DW video about a German-speaking city; Write a DACH 'top facts' list with superlatives; Daily Anki review

Topic: Media, Internet & Technology; Indirect Questions & da-/wo-Compounds
Vocabulary_Target: Media, smartphones, internet, social media, news
Grammar_Focus: Indirect questions (Können Sie mir sagen, wo/ob...); ob vs. wenn; da-/wo-compounds (darauf, worüber) vs. preposition + pronoun for people
Cultural_Focus: Data privacy (Datenschutz), the broadcasting fee, the Tagesschau ritual, phone contracts
Prompt_Text: Week 22, A2. Teach indirect questions with W-words and ob (Können Sie mir sagen, wann der Zug fährt? Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt), the difference between ob and wenn, and da-/wo-compounds (darauf, dafür, worüber, womit) for things vs. auf ihn / mit wem for people. Teach 80 words for media, smartphones, internet, social media and news. Create 10 dialogues: a tech-support hotline, setting up a phone contract, discussing a news story, a parent and teenager arguing about screen time. Explain German media and internet culture: strong attitudes to data privacy (Datenschutz), the public broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag), the Tagesschau as a ritual, and phone contract habits.
Practice_Prompt: Act as a polite hotline employee for an internet provider. I call about a problem. Make me use at least 6 indirect questions and da-/wo-compounds. Correct me afterwards and show a more polite native version of each request.
Self_Study_Instructions: Watch 'Tagesschau in 100 Sekunden' daily; Read 2 articles on nachrichtenleicht.de (easy-language news); Switch one social-media app to German; Daily Anki review

Topic: Environment & Future Plans; Futur I, zu-Infinitive, um...zu
Vocabulary_Target: Environment, recycling, energy, transport, sustainability, plans
Grammar_Focus: Futur I (werden + infinitive) vs. present for plans; infinitive with zu (vorhaben, versuchen, Lust haben...); um...zu for purpose
Cultural_Focus: Waste separation (color-coded bins), Pfand, Energiewende basics, cycling culture
Prompt_Text: Week 23, A2. Teach Futur I (werden + infinitive) for predictions and promises vs. the present tense for plans, the infinitive with zu after common verbs and expressions (vorhaben, versuchen, vergessen, Lust haben, Es ist wichtig, ...), and um...zu for purpose. Teach 80 words for environment, recycling, energy, transport and sustainability. Create 10 dialogues: a new flatmate learning the bin system, a sustainability discussion at work, planning a car-free holiday, New Year's resolutions. Explain German environmental culture: waste separation with color-coded bins, Pfand, the basics of the Energiewende, cycling culture, and how Germany, Austria and Switzerland compare.
Practice_Prompt: Give me 10 everyday items (a pizza box, a glass jar, batteries...). I tell you which bin each goes in and why, using um...zu or zu-infinitives. Then ask me 5 questions about my plans for next year, which I answer in Futur I. Correct everything.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 10 plans/resolutions using werden and zu-infinitives; Look up a German city's waste-separation guide; Listen to DW 'Langsam gesprochene Nachrichten' daily; Daily Anki review

Topic: A2 Review & Goethe A2 Mock Exam
Vocabulary_Target: Review of all A2 vocabulary (~1,700 words total)
Grammar_Focus: All A2 grammar: Perfekt/Präteritum, two-way prepositions, subordinate clauses, dative verbs, adjective endings, reflexive verbs, verbs with prepositions, comparison, indirect questions, Futur I, zu-infinitive
Cultural_Focus: Cultural check: daily life, festivals, work and housing in DACH
Prompt_Text: Week 24, A2 review. Based on the Goethe-Zertifikat A2 format, create a full mock exam: Lesen, Hören (as transcripts I can read aloud or record), Schreiben (an SMS and a semi-formal email of 30-40 words each) and Sprechen (asking and answering questions, talking about your life, planning something together). Then give me a one-page summary of all A2 grammar (Perfekt/Präteritum, two-way prepositions, subordinate clauses, dative verbs, adjective endings, reflexive verbs, verbs with prepositions, comparatives, indirect questions, Futur I, zu-infinitive), a 150-word review of the most-forgotten vocabulary from weeks 12-23, and a 20-question culture quiz. Don't show answers until I submit. Then diagnose my errors by category and give me a personal fix list before B1.
Practice_Prompt: Simulate the A2 speaking task where we plan something together: we need to buy a farewell gift for a colleague and find a time to meet. Then grade me with the official criteria (task completion, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation).
Self_Study_Instructions: Do the official free Goethe A2 practice test, timed; Write 3 emails (formal, semi-formal, informal) and get them corrected; Re-read your Perfekt diary from week 12 and correct your old mistakes; Optional: book the real A2 exam as a milestone

Topic: Stories & Fairy Tales; Präteritum of All Verbs
Vocabulary_Target: Storytelling, fairy tales, sequencing words
Grammar_Focus: Präteritum of regular and irregular verbs; written vs. spoken past; sequencing (zuerst, danach, plötzlich, schließlich)
Cultural_Focus: The Brothers Grimm, the German Fairy Tale Route, fairy-tale motifs in modern culture
Prompt_Text: Week 25, B1. Teach the Präteritum of regular and irregular verbs (machte, ging, kam, sah, nahm...) with the 80 most common irregular forms grouped by pattern, and explain that it's the standard tense for written narration, news and stories while speech prefers Perfekt (with regional differences: northern Germany uses Präteritum more). Teach 100 words for storytelling, fairy tales and sequencing (zuerst, danach, plötzlich, schließlich, am Ende). Write a simplified B1 retelling of 'Hänsel und Gretel' with a vocabulary list, then 3 short modern news-style texts. Explain the Brothers Grimm's role in German culture and language, the Deutsche Märchenstraße, and how fairy-tale motifs appear in modern German culture.
Practice_Prompt: Start a story in German Präteritum with two sentences. We continue it alternately, one sentence each, for 20 turns. Then correct all my Präteritum forms and rewrite my sentences in better narrative style.
Self_Study_Instructions: Read one simplified Grimm fairy tale per day; Rewrite a story you know in Präteritum (200 words); Verb trainer: 20 Präteritum forms/day; Listen to the Easy German Podcast regularly

Vocabulary_Target: Neighborhoods, community life, housing search, precise descriptions
Grammar_Focus: Relative pronouns in nominative/accusative/dative; with prepositions (in der, mit dem); dessen/deren; was and wo as relatives
Cultural_Focus: The Berlin 'Kiez', neighborhood help apps, gentrification debates, stairwell and courtyard etiquette
Prompt_Text: Week 26, B1. Teach relative clauses: relative pronouns in nominative, accusative and dative (der, den, dem, denen...), with prepositions (die Stadt, in der ich wohne), the genitive dessen/deren, and 'was' after alles/etwas/nichts and 'wo' for places. Show how to determine gender, case and number step by step. Teach 100 words for neighborhoods, community life, housing search and precise description. Create 8 dialogues and 2 short texts: describing your ideal neighborhood, a flat ad, a post on a neighborhood app, a dispute about a shared garden. Explain German neighborhood culture: the Kiez in Berlin, neighborhood-help apps like nebenan.de, gentrification debates, and the unwritten rules of stairwells and courtyards.
Practice_Prompt: Play 'Wer bin ich?': describe 10 objects, people or places to me using only relative clauses (Es ist ein Ding, mit dem man...). I guess. Then I do the same for 8 items. Correct my relative pronouns with a case explanation for each.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 15 dictionary-style definitions using relative clauses; Read 2 articles on nachrichtenleicht.de and underline every relative clause; Watch DW Nicos Weg B1 or an Easy German video; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Wishes, dreams, life decisions, advice, politeness
Grammar_Focus: Konjunktiv II: würde + infinitive and one-word forms (wäre, hätte, könnte, müsste, sollte, dürfte, wüsste, käme, ginge); unreal conditions; wishes; polite requests; advice
Cultural_Focus: Politeness through Konjunktiv II, directness vs. rudeness, emigration and immigration
Prompt_Text: Week 27, B1. Teach Konjunktiv II in the present: würde + infinitive, the common one-word forms (wäre, hätte, könnte, müsste, sollte, dürfte, wüsste, käme, ginge), unreal conditions (Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich...), wishes (Ich wünschte..., Wenn ich doch...!), polite requests (Könnten Sie...? Hätten Sie...?) and advice (An deiner Stelle würde ich..., Du solltest...). Teach 100 words for wishes, dreams, life decisions and advice. Create 8 dialogues and 2 texts: what you'd do with a lottery win, an advice column, polite requests at a government office, a friend considering emigrating. Explain how politeness works in German (Konjunktiv II as a softener), why German directness isn't rudeness, and the culture of Germans emigrating (Auswandern) and of immigration to Germany.
Practice_Prompt: Write me 3 letters to an advice column from fictional people with problems. I answer each with advice using Konjunktiv II. Then send me 10 blunt requests and I rewrite them politely. Correct and upgrade my versions.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 15 'Wenn ich... wäre/hätte' sentences about your dreams; Convert 10 imperatives into polite Konjunktiv II requests; Read one advice column in a German magazine online; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Science, inventions, technology, production processes, recipes
Grammar_Focus: Vorgangspassiv in Präsens, Präteritum, Perfekt (wird / wurde / ist ... worden); von vs. durch; impersonal passive
Cultural_Focus: German inventions, 'Made in Germany', engineering and Mittelstand culture
Prompt_Text: Week 28, B1. Teach the passive voice (Vorgangspassiv) in Präsens, Präteritum and Perfekt (wird gebaut, wurde gebaut, ist gebaut worden), von vs. durch, and when Germans prefer the passive (processes, news, instructions, when the actor doesn't matter). Teach 100 words for science, inventions, technology and production processes. Create 4 dialogues and 6 short texts: how bread / beer / chocolate is made, a factory tour, a museum guide explaining famous German-speaking inventions (printing press, automobile, aspirin, MP3), a recipe in the passive. Explain the story of 'Made in Germany' (originally a British warning label), German engineering and Mittelstand culture, and famous German-speaking scientists.
Practice_Prompt: Give me 10 active sentences from news headlines and I transform them into the passive, keeping the tense. Then ask me to explain a process I know well (e.g. a dish from my country) in the passive. Correct me.
Self_Study_Instructions: Describe a production process from your country in the passive (150 words); Read about 3 inventions on the Deutsches Museum website in German; Watch one 'Sendung mit der Maus' Sachgeschichte; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Life events, biographies, history, dates
Grammar_Focus: Temporal clauses (als vs. wenn, während, bevor, nachdem, seit(dem), bis, sobald); Plusquamperfekt with nachdem
Cultural_Focus: Erinnerungskultur (Stolpersteine, memorials), division and reunification, Ostalgie, Austria's and Switzerland's paths
Prompt_Text: Week 29, B1. Teach temporal subordinate clauses (als vs. wenn for the past, während, bevor, nachdem, seit/seitdem, bis, sobald) and the Plusquamperfekt (hatte gemacht, war gegangen) with the nachdem tense rule. Teach 100 words for biographies, life events and history. Write 3 short biographies (Albert Einstein, Sophie Scholl, Angela Merkel) and a short B1 text about the fall of the Berlin Wall and reunification. Explain German Erinnerungskultur (how Germany deals with its Nazi past: Stolpersteine, memorials, education), division and reunification, Ostalgie, and briefly how Austria's and Switzerland's 20th-century histories differ. Keep the history factual and balanced.
Practice_Prompt: Interview me about my life as if for a biography: 10 questions that require als, nachdem, bevor, während, seit. Then write my answers as a short third-person biography in Präteritum/Plusquamperfekt and mark what you corrected.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write your own biography (200 words) using 6 different temporal conjunctions; Watch a DW documentary on 1989 with German audio and subtitles; Read about Stolpersteine and find out whether a city you know has them; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Booking, travel problems, complaints, compensation, formal letter phrases
Grammar_Focus: Genitive case (des Mannes, der Frau); genitive prepositions (wegen, trotz, während, statt, innerhalb, außerhalb, aufgrund); von + dative in speech
Cultural_Focus: Complaint culture (direct but formal), train passenger rights, structure of a formal German letter
Prompt_Text: Week 30, B1. Teach the genitive case (articles, -s/-es endings, n-nouns), genitive prepositions (wegen, trotz, während, statt, innerhalb, außerhalb, aufgrund) and when spoken German uses von + dative instead. Teach 100 words for booking, travel problems, complaints and compensation, plus 20 fixed phrases for formal letters (Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, Hiermit möchte ich mich beschweren, Ich erwarte..., Mit freundlichen Grüßen). Create 6 dialogues and 4 texts: a complaint at a hotel reception, a train passenger asking for compensation, a formal complaint email to an airline, a customer-service reply. Explain German complaint culture (direct but formal), passenger rights for train delays (Fahrgastrechte), and the structure of a formal German letter, a typical B1 exam writing task.
Practice_Prompt: Give me a B1-exam-style writing task: a formal complaint about a holiday that went wrong (4 content points, ~100 words). I write it; you grade it like a Goethe B1 examiner, then show me a model answer at my level.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 2 formal complaint emails and get them corrected; Read the passenger-rights page on bahn.de; Genitive-preposition drills 10 min/day; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Education, university, vocational training, courses, skills
Grammar_Focus: sowohl...als auch, weder...noch, nicht nur...sondern auch, entweder...oder, zwar...aber, je...desto
Cultural_Focus: Dual vocational training (Ausbildung), mostly tuition-free universities, Fachhochschulen, Volkshochschule
Prompt_Text: Week 31, B1. Teach two-part conjunctions (sowohl...als auch, weder...noch, nicht nur...sondern auch, entweder...oder, zwar...aber, je...desto/umso) and their effect on word order. Teach 100 words for education, university, vocational training, courses and skills. Create 6 dialogues and 4 texts: a meeting with a student advisor, choosing between Ausbildung and university, enrolling in a Volkshochschule course, a forum discussion about lifelong learning. Explain the German education path after school: the dual vocational training system and why it's admired abroad, the Abitur, (mostly) tuition-free public universities, Fachhochschulen, the Volkshochschule and continuing education; compare Austria and Switzerland.
Practice_Prompt: Let's discuss 'Studium oder Ausbildung - was ist besser?' Ask for my opinion, push back with counterarguments, and require me to use at least 6 two-part conjunctions. Then give me feedback and a list of better phrases I could have used.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 200 words comparing education in your country and Germany using two-part conjunctions; Watch a German-language video about the 'Duale Ausbildung'; Read a German university's 'Studium' info page; Daily Anki review

Topic: Emotions & Mental Health; Prepositional Verbs, Adjectives & Nouns
Vocabulary_Target: Emotions, stress, mental health, wellbeing
Grammar_Focus: Adjectives and nouns with prepositions (stolz auf, zufrieden mit, Angst vor, Lust auf); review of verb + preposition; da-compounds introducing clauses (Ich freue mich darauf, dass...)
Cultural_Focus: Changing attitudes to mental health, burnout discourse, the Kur, access to psychotherapy, Gemütlichkeit
Prompt_Text: Week 32, B1. Teach adjectives and nouns with fixed prepositions (stolz auf, zufrieden mit, abhängig von, Angst vor, Lust auf, Interesse an) and review the 40 most important verb + preposition pairs. Teach the pattern with da-compounds that introduce clauses (Ich freue mich darauf, dass... / Ich habe Angst davor, zu...). Teach 100 words for emotions, stress, mental health and wellbeing. Create 6 dialogues and 4 texts: talking to a stressed friend, a doctor conversation about burnout, a magazine article about stress at work, a blog post about Gemütlichkeit. Explain German attitudes toward mental health (more open than before, the burnout discourse), the Kur tradition, how psychotherapy is accessed through health insurance, and the concepts Gemütlichkeit and Feierabend.
Practice_Prompt: Give me 15 sentences with the preposition missing (Ich bin stolz ___ meinen Sohn). Then ask me 8 personal questions about what I'm afraid of, proud of, happy about and interested in; I answer using da-compound + clause structures. Correct everything.
Self_Study_Instructions: Make an Anki deck of 60 verb/adjective/noun + preposition + case; Write a 150-word journal entry about your feelings this week; Listen to a German podcast episode about stress or mental health; Daily Anki review

Topic: Office & Business Communication; n-Declension & Formal Register
Vocabulary_Target: Office, meetings, projects, emails, phone calls
Grammar_Focus: n-declension (der Kollege - den Kollegen, der Kunde, der Name); formal register; Konjunktiv II politeness at work
Cultural_Focus: Sie vs. du at work, titles (Herr Dr.), punctuality, agendas and minutes, direct feedback, email etiquette
Prompt_Text: Week 33, B1. Teach the n-declension (masculine nouns like der Kollege, der Kunde, der Mensch, der Herr, der Name, der Student that add -(e)n outside the nominative) with the 40 most common ones. Teach formal workplace register: email openings and closings, phone phrases (Ich verbinde Sie, Kann ich etwas ausrichten?), making suggestions in meetings, and disagreeing politely. Teach 100 words for office, meetings, projects, emails and phone calls. Create 6 dialogues and 4 emails: rescheduling a meeting, a phone call with a client, asking a colleague for help, a meeting with a disagreement. Explain German workplace culture: Sie vs. du, titles (Herr Dr. Müller), punctuality, agendas and minutes, separating work and private life, direct feedback, and email etiquette.
Practice_Prompt: Simulate a workday: send me 4 emails from colleagues and clients (a request, a complaint, a meeting invitation, a question). I reply to each formally. Then grade my replies on register, structure and grammar and rewrite one as a model.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write 5 work emails for real situations from your job in German; Make n-declension flashcards; Watch a German video about business etiquette (Business-Knigge); Daily Anki review

Topic: Politics & Society; Passive with Modals & Passive Alternatives
Vocabulary_Target: Politics, government, elections, rights, the EU
Grammar_Focus: Passive with modal verbs (muss geändert werden); alternatives: man, sich lassen, -bar adjectives, sein + zu
Cultural_Focus: Federal system (Bund, Länder, Bundestag, Bundesrat), two-vote elections, coalitions, Swiss direct democracy, Austria's system, the EU (all presented neutrally)
Prompt_Text: Week 34, B1. Teach the passive with modal verbs (Das muss geändert werden, Das kann nicht bezahlt werden) and passive alternatives: man, sich lassen (Das lässt sich lösen), -bar adjectives (machbar, lösbar), and sein + zu (Der Antrag ist bis Freitag einzureichen). Teach 100 words for politics, government, elections, rights and the EU. Create 4 dialogues and 6 short texts: explaining how elections work, a citizens' meeting about a local issue, a news report about a new law, an interview about voting. Explain neutrally: Germany's federal system (Bund, Länder, Bundestag, Bundesrat, Chancellor vs. President), the two-vote election system, coalition governments, Austria's system, Switzerland's direct democracy (popular votes), and the EU. Present political parties factually without taking sides.
Practice_Prompt: Give me 10 problems in a fictional town (the bridge is broken, the school is too small...). I say what must / should / can be done using modal passive and alternatives (sich lassen, -bar). Then let's discuss one local issue for 10 turns; correct me afterwards.
Self_Study_Instructions: Read the easy-language election pages of the Federal Agency for Civic Education (bpb.de); Watch 'logo!' (children's news) or 'Tagesschau in 100 Sekunden'; Rewrite 10 active rules using passive alternatives; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Money, banking, saving, shopping decisions, contracts, insurance
Grammar_Focus: Konjunktiv II past (hätte gekauft, wäre gefahren); with modals (hätte ... sollen); concessive obwohl and trotzdem
Cultural_Focus: Saving culture, cash, the Schufa credit score, many insurances (Haftpflicht), contract cancellation, Sparkassen
Prompt_Text: Week 35, B1. Teach Konjunktiv II in the past (hätte gekauft, wäre gefahren), with modal verbs (hätte sparen sollen - the double infinitive) for regrets and alternatives, plus concessive obwohl and trotzdem. Teach 100 words for money, banking, saving, shopping decisions, contracts and insurance. Create 6 dialogues and 4 texts: opening a bank account, regretting an online purchase, cancelling a gym contract (Kündigung), a forum post about saving money. Explain German money culture: the love of saving, cash use, the Schufa credit score, why Germans have so many insurances (especially Haftpflicht), long contracts and how cancellation works, and the role of Sparkassen. Compare with Austria and Switzerland.
Practice_Prompt: Tell me 6 short stories of bad decisions (someone bought a too-expensive car, missed a flight...). For each, I say what the person should have done differently (hätte... sollen, wäre...). Then ask me about 3 decisions in my life I'd make differently. Correct me.
Self_Study_Instructions: Write a formal Kündigung letter for a fictional contract; Write 10 sentences about regrets and alternatives; Read a German personal-finance article (e.g. on finanztip.de); Daily Anki review

Topic: Energy & Sustainability; Participles as Adjectives & Infinitive Clauses
Vocabulary_Target: Energy, climate, sustainability, consumption, mobility
Grammar_Focus: Present and past participles as adjectives (die steigenden Preise, das gebrauchte Fahrrad); ohne...zu, (an)statt...zu; ohne dass / statt dass
Cultural_Focus: Energiewende, nuclear phase-out, balcony solar, e-mobility, Germany's climate-policy debates (all sides)
Prompt_Text: Week 36, B1. Teach present and past participles used as adjectives (die steigenden Preise, das gebrauchte Fahrrad) with correct adjective endings, and the infinitive constructions ohne...zu and (an)statt...zu, plus ohne dass / statt dass when the subjects differ. Teach 100 words for energy, climate, sustainability, consumption and mobility. Create 4 dialogues and 6 texts: a debate between neighbors about solar panels, a news article on the Energiewende, a blog about living without a car, a consumer-advice text. Explain the Energiewende and the nuclear phase-out, balcony solar systems (Balkonkraftwerk), e-mobility, and present the main positions in Germany's climate-policy debate fairly, including disagreements about costs and speed.
Practice_Prompt: Give me 10 sentence pairs to combine using participle adjectives (Die Preise steigen. Die Preise sind ein Problem. - Die steigenden Preise...). Then I argue for or against a car-free city center in 8 sentences using ohne...zu / statt...zu. Correct and improve my style.
Self_Study_Instructions: Read 2 'Top-Thema' articles on DW Deutsch lernen; Write a 200-word opinion on one sustainability measure; Participle drills 10 min/day; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Discussion phrases, opinions, media, social debates
Grammar_Focus: Connectors (einerseits...andererseits, außerdem, deshalb, folglich, trotzdem, dennoch, im Gegensatz dazu); opinion phrases; presentation structure
Cultural_Focus: German 'Streitkultur', talk-show debates, fact-based argument; B1 exam presentation format
Prompt_Text: Week 37, B1. Teach how to give and support opinions, agree and disagree (politely and strongly), and structure arguments with connectors (einerseits...andererseits, außerdem, deshalb, folglich, trotzdem, dennoch, im Gegensatz dazu, zum Beispiel). Topic: Natural Spoken German; Modal Particles & Regional Varieties
Vocabulary_Target: Colloquial expressions, fillers, Austrian and Swiss Standard German words
Grammar_Focus: Modal particles (doch, ja, mal, eben, halt, eigentlich, denn, schon, wohl, bloß); spoken contractions and fillers

Prompt_Text: Week 42, B2. Teach the 10 most important modal particles (doch, ja, mal, eben, halt, eigentlich, denn, schon, wohl, bloß): for each, its effect, 4 natural example sentences with the nuance explained, and the same sentence without the particle for contrast. Practice_Prompt: Write 10 neutral sentences; I add the right modal particle to change the tone (friendly, impatient, reassuring...). Self_Study_Instructions: Watch 3 Easy German street interviews and note the particles; Listen to an Austrian (Ö1 or FM4) and a Swiss (SRF) program for 15 min each; Shadow 5 min of natural dialogue daily; Daily Anki review

Topic: Crime, Mysteries & Speculation; Subjective Modal Verbs & Futur II
Vocabulary_Target: Crime, investigation, police, mysteries
Grammar_Focus: Subjective modal verbs (muss, dürfte, kann/könnte, soll, will) in present and past; werden for assumptions; Futur II
Cultural_Focus: The 'Tatort' Sunday ritual, regional crime novels, German true-crime podcasts
Prompt_Text: Week 43, B2. Teach the subjective use of modal verbs to express certainty and hearsay - muss (almost certain), dürfte (probable), kann/könnte (possible), soll (reportedly), will (claims) - in the present and past (Er muss den Schlüssel verloren haben), plus werden for assumptions and Futur II (Sie wird schon nach Hause gegangen sein). Show a certainty scale. Teach 120 words for crime, investigation, police and mysteries. Write a short B2 crime story in 3 parts where clues are revealed gradually and the characters speculate, plus a police report and a newspaper report on the same case. Explain the Tatort phenomenon (the Sunday-night ritual since 1970, each city with its own team), regional crime novels (Regionalkrimi), and the popularity of German true-crime podcasts.
Practice_Prompt: Give me a mystery: clues about a missing person, one at a time. After each clue I speculate in German using subjective modals and Futur II at different certainty levels. At the end, reveal the solution and correct my speculation sentences.
Self_Study_Instructions: Watch one Tatort episode (ARD Mediathek) with German subtitles; Write a 250-word crime story using subjective modals; Listen to one episode of a German true-crime podcast; Daily Anki review

Topic: Business & Economy; Advanced Connectors & Text Cohesion
Vocabulary_Target: Economy, business, companies, markets, negotiation
Grammar_Focus: Advanced connectors (zumal, sofern, insofern als, wohingegen, indem, sodass, als ob, je nachdem, geschweige denn); cohesion (dies, dabei, letzterer)

Vocabulary_Target: Specialized vocabulary from your own field

Topic: Law, Rights & Everyday Legal Situations; Zustandspassiv & lassen
Vocabulary_Target: Law, rights, contracts, tenancy, consumer protection

Self_Study_Instructions: Read Articles 1-20 of the Grundgesetz in German (freely available online); Read a consumer-advice page on verbraucherzentrale.de; Write a formal objection letter (Widerspruch) for a fictional case; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Literary and film analysis, idioms, collocations

Vocabulary_Target: Demographics and pensions, housing, digitalization, migration and integration, climate policy

Self_Study_Instructions: Write 2 essays (200-300 words) and get them corrected; Watch a segment of a German political talk show and note argument phrases; Read a 'Pro und Contra' piece on each debate topic; Daily Anki review

Vocabulary_Target: Politeness, softening, criticism, refusing, apologizing, small talk

Prompt_Text: Week 50, B2. Teach 100 words and phrases for these speech acts. Create 10 mini-scenarios where the 'textbook' answer would sound odd and show what a native speaker would actually say. Rate each response for appropriateness (too blunt / too vague / just right) and show a native alternative.
Self_Study_Instructions: Note 10 real situations this week where you'd soften, criticize or refuse, and write the German phrasing; Watch a video comparing German and other communication styles; Do a Tandem session focused on giving feedback; Daily Anki review
